acceptance_checks: Regression coverage proves that an arbitrary value at `sys.path[0]` survives `modify_sys_path()`.
Coverage proves that, with an arbitrary first entry and a leading-colon `PYTHONPATH`, the arbitrary entry survives while only the applicable following exact cwd entry is removed.
Coverage proves that, with an arbitrary first entry and a trailing-colon `PYTHONPATH`, the arbitrary entry survives while only the applicable exact cwd entry is removed.
Existing covered behavior for removing exact `""`, `"."`, or exact `os.getcwd()` current-directory entries remains passing.
Existing covered explicit-current-directory `PYTHONPATH` exception behavior remains passing.
Existing covered retention of trailing working-directory entries used by editable installations remains passing.
Existing path-stripping and local-plugin import integration tests remain passing.
confirmed_decisions: The removable first-entry set is exactly `""`, `"."`, and the exact string returned by `os.getcwd()`; no normalization, resolution, case folding, or symlink equivalence is authorized.

If an arbitrary `sys.path[0]` is preserved, leading- or trailing-colon `PYTHONPATH` handling must preserve that prefix and remove only the applicable exact current-directory entry introduced by the empty component.
The change is limited to `modify_sys_path()` and its `python -m pylint`/`runpy` path; installed console-script behavior is out of scope.
Existing exact empty-string/cwd removals, explicit-cwd `PYTHONPATH` exceptions, and retained trailing cwd entries for editable installations remain compatible behavior.
The owner accepts retention of cwd-equivalent but non-exact path spellings as a bounded residual risk.
The complete contract was explicitly approved by the owner.
summary: Change only `pylint.modify_sys_path()` behavior used by `python -m pylint` and `runpy`, with minimum regression coverage. Remove `sys.path[0]` only when its value is exactly `""`, `"."`, or exactly equal to `os.getcwd()`; preserve every other first entry, including paths merely equivalent after normalization, resolution, case conversion, or symlink traversal. When an arbitrary first entry is preserved and `PYTHONPATH` begins or ends with a colon, preserve that arbitrary entry while removing only the applicable exact current-directory entry introduced by the empty PYTHONPATH component. Retain established removals for existing exact-empty-string/current-working-directory cases, explicit-current-directory `PYTHONPATH` exceptions, and trailing working-directory entries used by editable installations. Exclude changes to console-script behavior, path normalization or equivalence matching, unrelated import handling, supported environments, and public APIs. Internal control flow and test-fixture organization remain implementation discretion provided removals are value-qualified, safe for exercised path shapes, and all acceptance checks pass. Accepted residual risk: unusual uncited `sys.path` layouts may retain cwd-equivalent entries not matching the approved exact values, intentionally avoiding broader deletion behavior.
